If I could make one change in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, it would be to disable the new swipe-down gesture for invoking Siri AI. There are already more than enough ways to summon Siri without breaking the muscle memory I have for opening the notification center on my iPhone and iPad.

Meanwhile, on the Mac side, macOS 27 Golden Gate is almost entirely good news. Even at the end of August, new betas are still adding welcome changes. That said, there is one change I would still like to see before macOS 27 ships next month.

MacBook battery percentage is harder to read in macOS 27 Golden Gate

macOS 27 Golden Gate includes a redesigned menu bar battery control. By default, the percentage is not shown—only a battery-shaped visual indicator icon.

In that state, it looks fine. I have percentage display turned off on my iPhone as well, using the same battery indicator icon. But on the Mac I have always preferred to show the percentage.

If you turn on the "Show Percentage" option in macOS 27 Golden Gate, the number appears inside the battery icon. I assume this is for consistency with what iPhone is doing in iOS 27.

Putting the percentage inside the battery icon on iPhone was Apple's way of dealing with the spatial density issue of fitting everything to the right of the notch or Dynamic Island. On the Mac, even in the menu bar, that screen-space problem does not really exist for me.

I have been running macOS 27 Golden Gate on a 15-inch MacBook Air since day one of the first developer beta. I have noticed that I check the battery percentage far less often, because it is not as easy on my eyes to read.

I hope Apple reconsiders this design decision in the future, especially if more users run into the same issue. In the meantime, I have at least solved the problem for myself.

I used Codex to make a simple menu bar utility that displays the current battery status and percentage clearly and reliably, with the visual clarity I was looking for. If you think this would help you too, you can download and install it for free here.
